title: Isolation and Flow Cytometric Analysis of Interstitial Macrophages in Murine Lung Models
author: Jeong, Seok

steps.title: Thaw frozen cancer cells
steps.instruction: Warm a 37 °C water bath, place a cryovial containing 1.5–2 × 10⁶ LLC or 4T1 cells in 5 % DMSO/95 % FBS and thaw quickly; transfer the entire volume into 9 mL pre‑warmed culture medium in a 15 mL tube; centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min, discard supernatant containing DMSO.

steps.title: Seed cells in T‑75 flask
steps.instruction: Add 15 mL fresh culture medium to a T‑75 flask, resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL medium, and seed 1.5 × 10⁶ cells per flask. Prepare 27 µL of 0.2 % trypan‑blue (diluted in 1X PBS) in a 1.5 mL tube, mix 3 µL of the cell suspension with the dye, load 10 µL into a hemocytometer, count cells in at least two corner or center squares, multiply the average count by 10⁵ to obtain total cells, and verify viability > 80 %. Incubate the flask at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C for 2 days.

steps.title: Subculture cancer cells
steps.instruction: Aspirate spent medium (collect floating LLC cells if desired and centrifuge to recover them); wash adherent cells with 10 mL sterile 1X PBS; add 1 mL trypsin‑EDTA, spread to cover the monolayer and incubate at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C for 2 min (LLC) or 5 min (4T1); add 9 mL fresh medium, transfer the suspension to a 15 mL tube, ensure complete detachment, centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min; add 15 mL fresh medium to a new T‑75 flask, resuspend the pellet in 1 mL medium, seed 1.5 × 10⁶ viable cells per flask (viability > 80 %), and incubate 2 days. Perform at least two subcultures before mouse injection and confirm mycoplasma‑free status by PCR.

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension for injection
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium, wash cells once with 10 mL sterile 1X PBS, add 1 mL trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 2 min (LLC) or 5 min (4T1) at 5 % CO₂, 37 °C; add 9 mL medium, transfer to a 15 mL tube, centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant, add 1 mL ice‑cold 1X PBS, then add 9 mL ice‑cold 1X PBS and centrifuge again at 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C; verify live (trypan‑blue‑negative) cells > 95 %; resuspend at 5 × 10⁵ cells/200 µL for LLC or 1 × 10⁶ cells/100 µL for 4T1 in ice‑cold 1X PBS; aliquot 1 mL into 1.5 mL tubes, keep on ice (max 2 h).

steps.title: Euthanize mice
steps.instruction: Terminate each mouse using an appropriate method (e.g., isoflurane drop jar or 2–3 ×  overdose of injectable anesthetic) one at a time.

steps.title: Perfuse lungs with PBS
steps.instruction: Load a 10 mL syringe with PBS, replace the syringe needle with a 26‑gauge needle, insert a second 26‑gauge needle into the inferior vena cava (under the liver) to serve as outflow, and inject PBS into the right ventricle to flush the pulmonary circulation.

steps.title: Place lungs on ice
steps.instruction: Transfer the perfused lungs into 5 mL HBSS placed in a 5 mL tube and keep on ice.

steps.title: Mince lungs in collagenase
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL collagenase solution to a 60 × 75 mm Petri dish, tilt the dish so the liquid pools on one side, and mince the lungs on the dry side with curved scissors, keeping cut pieces on the dry side; add an additional 3.5 mL collagenase solution, pipette thoroughly with a 1000 µL tip to resuspend tissue, and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min, pipetting again at the 15‑min mark with a 200 µL tip to aid dissociation.

steps.title: Inactivate collagenase
steps.instruction: Add cold DMEM or RPMI containing 10 % FBS at twice the digestion volume (8 mL) to the suspension; optionally add 0.5 mM EDTA.

steps.title: Filter and dilute cell suspension
steps.instruction: Pass the suspension through a 70 µm nylon mesh into a 50 mL conical tube; add PBS to bring the total volume to 50 mL.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate the supernatant.

steps.title: Lyse red blood cells with ACK
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL ACK lysis buffer, add 3 mL additional ACK buffer, incubate 4 min at room temperature (warm ACK to 36 °C before use).

steps.title: Wash post‑lysis cells
steps.instruction: Add PBS to bring the volume to 50 mL, centrifuge 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 1 mL PBS.

steps.title: Final filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the cell suspension again through a 70 µm nylon membrane into a 50 mL tube (or carefully into a 1.5 mL tube to avoid spillage).

steps.title: Aliquot cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Dispense 1 × 10⁶–5 × 10⁶ cells into each well of a 96‑well v‑bottom plate (use 1–5 × 10⁶ cells per well).

steps.title: Prepare staining controls
steps.instruction: Create unstained and single‑stained control wells by mixing aliquots from all samples; allocate one well per fluorochrome used, using the same antibody working concentration as in the fully stained samples.

steps.title: Centrifuge plate
steps.instruction: Balance the 96‑well plate and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Live/Dead staining
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL of Live/Dead dye (diluted 1:500–1:1000 in PBS) to each well, incubate 15 min at room temperature, protect from light by wrapping the plate in aluminum foil.

steps.title: Wash after viability stain
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, and wash cells with 200 µL FACS buffer; centrifuge again at 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Block Fc receptors
steps.instruction: Resuspend cells in 50 µL CD16/32 antibody diluted to 1 µg/mL in FACS buffer, incubate 15 min on ice.

steps.title: Surface marker staining
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C, then add 50 µL of conjugated surface‑marker antibodies diluted to their working concentrations in FACS buffer; if Brilliant Violet or Super Bright dyes are used, include 10 µL Brilliant Stain Buffer Plus per test (total 50 µL per well); incubate 30 min on ice in the dark.

steps.title: Wash post‑surface stain
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, wash with 200 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge again at 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Intracellular staining (optional)
steps.instruction: Fix cells by adding 200 µL IC Fixation Buffer, incubate 30 min on ice in the dark; centrifuge 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C, wash with 200 µL 1X permeabilization buffer, centrifuge again; add intracellular antibodies diluted in 1X permeabilization buffer (total 50 µL per well), incubate 30 min on ice in the dark; centrifuge 300 g for 5 min at 4 °C, wash with 200 µL 1X permeabilization buffer, centrifuge, resuspend in 200 µL FACS buffer, filter through a 70 µm cell strainer, transfer to FACS tubes and add an additional 100 µL FACS buffer.

steps.title: Run samples on flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Prime the BD LSRFortessa X‑20 or FACSymphony A3, enable FSC‑A/H and SSC‑A/H for doublet exclusion, set lasers: 405 nm for Zombie Aqua, eFluor 450‑CD11b, BV605‑Ly6C, SB780‑MerTK, BV421‑Siglec‑F; 488 nm for FITC‑Ly6G/CD3 and PerCP‑CD64; 637 nm for Alexa 700‑CD45 and APC‑eFluor 780‑MHC‑II; acquire 300 000 live events per sample, filter each sample before acquisition, monitor the “Time” plot for consistent flow, avoid air bubbles, export data as FCS files.

steps.title: Analyze flow data
steps.instruction: In FlowJo, gate FSC‑A vs FSC‑H to exclude doublets, gate live cells using unstained or FMO controls, gate CD45⁺ leukocytes, plot CD11b vs Ly6G/CD3 to exclude Ly6G⁺/CD3⁺ neutrophils/lymphocytes (select Ly6G⁻/CD3⁻), plot CD11b vs Ly6C to exclude monocytes, gate CD64⁺ MerTK⁺ double‑positive cells as pan‑macrophages, then plot CD11b vs Siglec‑F to distinguish interstitial macrophages (CD11b⁺ Siglec‑F⁻) from alveolar macrophages (CD11b⁻ Siglec‑F⁺); assess MHC‑II expression with a histogram or contour plot. Note: CD64⁺ MerTK⁺ is preferred over F4/80 for macrophage identification in LLC‑bearing lungs.

description: The lungs are a common site of metastatic tumor colonization, and macrophages have been shown to play a critical role in promoting metastatic progression.2 Pulmonary macrophages are broadly classified into two subsets: alveolar macrophages, which are easily obtained through bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid sampling due to their location in the alveoli3; and interstitial macrophages, which are embedded within the lung parenchyma and are considerably more difficult to isolate.4 Interstitial macrophages are derived from circulating monocytes and share phenotypic markers with other mononuclear cells, complicating their identification and analysis.5 This protocol describes a detailed method for the isolation of interstitial macrophages from metastasized murine lungs, as well as procedures for cell preparation and flow cytometric analysis.
